title: The Quackenbush Journeys, 1907–1908: an evidence-based reconstruction

authorship.historical writers: Verbatim blocks are the words of the historical correspondents as transcribed by the PI; her editorial marks ([sic], [?], [illeg], struck text, colour) are preserved.
authorship.principal investigator: Rebecca J. H. Woods (University of Toronto): transcription file, comprehensive and terse timelines, Cast of Characters, and the talk text “Time, Temperature, and Tissue in the Circumpolar North: A Tale of Two Mammoths” (MIT, 20 Sept 2019). Her summaries and editorial notes are typed and rendered separately from verbatim text.
authorship.gazetteers: USGS GNIS (Alaska domestic names file), Canadian Geographical Names Database, GeoNames; Wikidata as cross-check only.
authorship.model: Claude (Anthropic) built the data model, typed the blocks, normalised names, geocoded against gazetteers, wrote the geocoding and network rules, selected and ordered quotations, and wrote the short connective notes labelled “model”. It added no fact, date, coordinate or quotation that is not in the inputs or the named gazetteers.

block_types.verbatim: words of the historical writer, as transcribed
block_types.summary: the PI's paraphrase of a document
block_types.editorial: the PI's description of the physical document, archival context, or dated research note
block_types.annotation: a marginal or interlinear annotation on the original, as transcribed

status_chips.verified: attested name matched to an authoritative gazetteer record
status_chips.inferred: identification or date is a model inference from the described route or sequence
status_chips.approximate: placed from Quackenbush's distance/direction statements or a described relation to a named feature
status_chips.unlocated: cannot be placed from the sources
status_chips.naming: flag, not a status: two attested names denote one gazetteer point; records naming variance, not a dispute about position

unlocated_kinds.withheld: the location was deliberately not disclosed in the sources
unlocated_kinds.contradictory: the provided statements place it differently and cannot be reconciled
unlocated_kinds.ambiguous: the attested name has several gazetteer homonyms, or the reading of the name is uncertain
unlocated_kinds.not_geocoded: outside the journey; no gazetteer was consulted for it in this build

constraint_kinds.distance: a stated distance in miles from a located anchor — drawn as a dashed ring around the anchor; no point
constraint_kinds.near: a stated nearness without a distance — drawn as a leader label at the anchor; no radius
constraint_kinds.identity: a statement equating the place with a located one — drawn as a bracket at that place; nothing asserted

geocoding_tiers.1: published coordinates in the sources — none exist
geocoding_tiers.2: authoritative gazetteers (GNIS, CGNDB, GeoNames; Wikidata cross-check)
geocoding_tiers.3: historical maps/charts — none available (1906 Post Route Map not provided)
geocoding_tiers.5: approximate placement with large uncertainty radius

quotation_classes.tie evidence: every quotation on a stated / PI / affiliation tie is found verbatim in the sources (build fails otherwise)
quotation_classes.funding: every funding edge quotes a sum or promise verbatim
quotation_classes.Tale excerpts: every story excerpt is an exact substring of the Tale and ends at a sentence or quotation boundary
quotation_classes.Cast lines and characterisations: every pi_characterisation and characterisation is a verbatim line of the PI's texts
quotation_classes.quoted fragments in authored prose: 459 quoted spans in model notes, place/stop/segment fields, findings, roles, variants, addresses, institutions, published excerpts and notes, tie labels, and record notes are verified (allow-list of quoted vocabulary, none of it currently needed: approximate, disputed, inferred, model, unlocated, verified, via PI)
